When he told me this, I dove waaaaay too deep into nutrigenic/nutrigenomic theories. Basically, during replication of DNA, nutrients can alter how the DNA from the original cell is transcribed to the daughter cells. Things like vitamin C or certain amino acids can change the transcription of DNA. It takes 2 or more generations for a genetic mutation to appear, so whatever we are doing to our bodies now will alter our grandchildren's DNA. This could be like how the body distributes fat; if you consume a ton of trans fats, your grandchildren could "adapt" by carrying more weight in their midsection. This is a theory of mine because of how the hourglass figure was much more common in women a century ago, but now only 1 in 8 women have the hourglass proportions. However, for the individual, poor diet can lead to poor DNA replication, leading to premature aging and being susceptible to more diseases. This is a mix of things I've learned from lectures and my own thoughts, so I could be wrong.

Anyway, the Baby Boomer generation was the first generation exposed to overly processed foods as children/young adults. I wonder if the junk food they consumed has altered DNA enough to be the cause of today's rise in allergies, asthma and autism. This altered DNA could also be the reason behind mental disorders and addictions of all kinds. I have a theory, once we know enough about genetics and nutrition: that when a baby is born, we will be able to get a sample of their DNA, and determine a healthy diet for that baby.
